inventory_summary: Inventoried: 62 ceilings and 296 wall ends by room occupancy/coat (probe p5-p9), 37 rooms' floor stacks and 40 door/opening floor pairs (p2), 138 drywall trim records, 5 paint-standard materials/15 paint products, the LVP selection (Karndean AKP-RL38), vinyl (Tarkett First Class), carpet/pad, tile stacks and 8 transition products. Web-checked: Karndean product page + rigid-core install guide (KD8132GLO, pdftotext), BM Ultra Spec 500 N538 TDS and N534 coverage, Tarkett First Class spec, DITRA-HEAT 5.5 mm, SurePly/Patriot 0.205 in, ClarkDietrich M401-10, USG Firecode C vs 1/2 in Type X, retail 1/4 in Z-bars. Sheets opened: A-002 p28, A-101 p29, A-102 p30, A-103 p31, A-104 p32, A-541 p92, A-542 p93, A-543 p94, A-544 p95, A-545 p96, A-546 p97, A-550 p101, A-603 p152, A-604 p153, plus A-519 p70, A-520 p71, A-530 p81 (text), A-567 p118, A-577 p128 (text). 10 prior ids re-probed; 7 new findings. haus check was not re-run (baseline checks.json read: 0 FAIL). NOT examined: Sweet Spot I carpet backing/total thickness and the Emphatic II carpet, the 3/8 in rebond pad manufacturer acceptance; Johnsonite/rubber cove base product and its 4 in vs 3.5 in height (O2 owns the base side); the stall-mat thickness (Tractor Supply 3/4 in tolerance vs the D-B-SAUNA reducer's 0.75 in maximum); PT-4 ADVANCE 793 / Emerald / Behr alternates' data sheets and the SW/Behr perm figures (paint note's own 'TBD' items); Behr drywall primer TDS (marked TBD in the product row); the opened-package order rounding (780 SF = 33.2 boxes, takeoff does not round to whole boxes); Fry Reglet profiles; Trim-Tex AS6010/8710/9010/7010 re-fetch (round 1 verified); remaining A-517..A-584 detail sheets beyond the ones listed (same patterns); gym base (A-603 lists none beside the 3/4 in mats; not judged); 3D viewer finishes.
verified_clean: PaintStandard picks (probe of all 296 non-foundation wall ends, +/-1 in off each face against claimed_room_faces): every gypsum face of a used room carries a coat (paint-wall 33 bedroom / 25 living / 33 storage / 16 hall ...; paint-wet on 35 bath and 4 laundry faces); the only bare gypsum faces are in the unpainted rooms RM-M-MECH, RM-B-FURNACE, RM-B-ESS, RM-A-POCKET, RM-A-EAST-UNFIN (and the shiplap/PVC/brick/plywood faces by design).

Unpainted rooms are really bare: ceilings of RM-M-MECH, RM-B-FURNACE, RM-A-POCKET, RM-A-EAST-UNFIN are plain gwb; exterior walls inside them keep PT-1 as the Class III retarder (A-603 RM-M-MECH 'gwb + PT-1').

All 62 ceilings: used rooms take paint-ceiling (PT-2) or paint-wet (baths/laundry); RM-B-SAUNA shiplap, RM-S-PLANT PVC, RM-B-ESS two Type X lids; only RM-GARAGE is primer-only (legacy gwb-primer, 523 SF, printed 'gwb + gwb-primer').

BM Ultra Spec 500 Eggshell N538 TDS (read from the 2019 N538 US sheet): 350-400 SF/gal, volume solids 42 +/- 2%, MPI 52/145, eggshell 10-12 @ 60, 'apply one or two coats', mildew resistance statement present -> PT-1 (and PT-3, same can) match note and A-604; N534 primer 350-400 SF/gal. A-604 (p153) table matches products_paint.py rows.

Karndean AKP-RL38 product page: 48 x 7 in, 7.0 mm, 30 mil, rigid core, 23.51 SF/box -> lvp finish_thickness_in 0.2756 (7.0/25.4) and floor +1.0256 in over joists; no heated floor under LVP (FloorHeat only in RM-M-BATH2, RM-S-BATH1); 3/16 in min gap, undercut/skirting rules and 85 F interface limit as the note states (KD8132GLO).

findings.title: D-M-MECH's west 15.5 in of threshold opens onto the FS-M-MECH deck void: no subfloor and no LVP under half the doorway

evidence.measured: FS-M-MECH.deck_voids has one void x 6.0..48.5 in, y 401.5..426.2 in (42.5 x 24.7 in). D-M-MECH spans x 33.0..65.2 in (RO 32.2 in) in W-M-MECH-S (y 400, 4.5 in thick), so 15.5 in of its width (x 33.0..48.5) sits over the void. surfaces_at(model,(41.1,402.8)) returns no FS-M-MECH surface (only the storeys above and below); at (57.2,402.8) it returns FS-M-MECH/RM-M-MECH lvp 1.026 in. DoorwayAssembly.adjacent_floors = (RM-M-MUDROOM lvp, None); unknown = 'floor varies across doorway side 1; split finish layout required' + 'adjacent walking surface or finish thickness is missing' (checks.json integrity.doorway_assembly UNKNOWN). The DU-ERV-OA riser (8 in at 3'-4", 33'-11") stands in the same west half. The note and TODO call this 'floor varies' but do not say there is no deck there.
evidence.expected: A mech-closet threshold with a continuous subfloor and plank across the full door width; risers pass through ~9-10 in sleeved holes, not a 42 x 25 in void that starts 1.5 in inside the door.
evidence.method: Probe /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-colincatlin-Documents-NoCloud-TypeHaus/fc951bd3-20bf-434f-9b45-0a1dac7cd982/scratchpad/geometry-review/I4/p16.py (doorway._floor_sample_stations + adjacent_floor at the 4 stations) and /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-colincatlin-Documents-NoCloud-TypeHaus/fc951bd3-20bf-434f-9b45-0a1dac7cd982/scratchpad/geometry-review/I4/p17.py (FS-M-MECH.deck_voids bounds, surfaces_at at 5 points).

findings.source: model: FS-M-MECH.deck_voids; storeys/main.py FO-M-ERV-OA comment block; floor_heights.md 'Still open'
findings.proposed_fix: Either trim the void/lid it: author a plywood cover (cut for the risers, fire-stopped per R302.11) under x 33..48.5 and let the LVP run to the threshold, or shift the door east / narrow the void to x >= 33 in. Then D-M-MECH gets an LVP-to-LVP doorway (step 0) and the TODO closes.

findings.title: Carpet Z-bar section floats 1/2 in above the subfloor it is 'fastened to', and a stock 1/4 in bar cannot leave the carpet flush with 3/4 in oak

evidence.measured: _zbar(): DoorwayProductSpec datum 'lower_floor' (the oak, 0.75 in above the subfloor), bar polygon z -0.25..0 relative to it, i.e. 0.50..0.75 in above the subfloor; product text says 'fastened to the subfloor against the hard floor's edge'. Carpet stack = 0.56 pile + 0.0625 backing + 0.375 cushion = 1.0 in; the note says the 0.62 in carpet is 'tucked flush with the 3/4 in hard floor', but a carpet 0.62 in thick tucked at the subfloor tops out at 0.62 in over it (0.13 in under the oak), and the carpet field stands 0.25 in over the oak. Retail Z-bars are about 1/4 in tall x 1 1/4 in wide (M-D 'Aluminum 0.25 in T x 1.25 in W x 48 in L Floor Z-bar', Lowe's 1000062539); the modelled bar is 0.25 x 0.75 in.
evidence.expected: A bar standing on the subfloor (z 0..0.25 in) with the carpet edge below its lip; the oak/carpet junction is a 1/4 in field rise to the oak plus a lipped edge, or a 3/4 in-high bar (not a stock part).
evidence.method: Read _zbar() and PROD-CARPET-ZBAR text; arithmetic from materials_flooring.py (1.0 in stack) and floor_heights.md; web: lowes.com/pd/M-D-Aluminum-0-25-in-T-x-1-25-in-W-x-48-in-L-Aluminum-Floor-Z-bar/1000062539.

findings.source: notes/bedroom_carpet.md ('Z-bar answer holds to 0.10 inch'); retail Z-bar listing above
findings.proposed_fix: Re-draw the bar on the subfloor (z -0.75..-0.50 rel. oak) and say in the product text that the carpet edge lands ~1/8 in under the oak lip, or buy a measured bar; keep the 0.25 in rise.

findings.title: Five walls specify 1/2 in 'gwb-x' (Type X); A-541/A-545/A-567 print 'gwb-x 1/2"', but the 1/2 in Type X board is Canadian: US stocks Firecode C

evidence.measured: Resolved wall layers: gwb-x on INT_2X4_STAGGERED_X_HALF is 0.500 in (walls W-M-LS, W-M-CLN, W-M-CLN2, W-S-SN1, W-S-SN2); every other gwb-x layer in the house is 0.625 in. The assembly source cites NRC test 'one layer 13 mm Type X gypsum each side' (a Canadian board). Search 2026-11-05: the only 1/2 in US board with a Type X rating is USG Sheetrock Firecode C (UL type C, ASTM C1396); UltraLight Firecode X is 5/8 in.
evidence.expected: A US-orderable 1/2 in part: gwb-c (the house already has it) with the STC cited as the Type X equivalent, or 5/8 in gwb-x and a 1/8 in thicker wall.
evidence.method: Probe /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-colincatlin-Documents-NoCloud-TypeHaus/fc951bd3-20bf-434f-9b45-0a1dac7cd982/scratchpad/geometry-review/I4/p10.py (gypsum layer thickness by assembly); web search USG Firecode C 1/2 in; sheets A-541 (p92), A-545 (p96), A-567 (p118) labels.

findings.source: partitions_half.py comment (NRC IR-761 TL-93-208, 13 mm Type X); https://www.usgme.com/default/sheetrock-brand-firecode-type-x-panels.html
findings.proposed_fix: Retype the two gwb-x layers of INT_2X4_STAGGERED_X_HALF to gwb-c and say 'Type C (US equivalent of the 13 mm Type X test board)' in the source; no geometry moves.

findings.title: lvp_flooring.md sizes the expansion gap off 'an area over 1000 SF' but the LVP field is 841 SF of rooms (709 SF net)

evidence.measured: A-603 LVP rooms: LIVING 701 + BATH1 20 + LAUNDRY 19 + MECH 10 + MUD-CLOSET 13 + MUDROOM 49 + PANTRY 13 + STUDY-CLOSET 16 = 841 SF; takeoff floor_finishes lvp net 708.9 SF (order 780). The note says 'the main floor is about 36 ft square ... its area is over 1000 SF: use the 5/16 in gap'. Karndean KD8132GLO (Jan 2024): 3/16 in (5 mm) minimum; 'must be increased to 5/16 in (8 mm) for areas larger than 1000 sq. ft.'; 5/16 in joint at runs over 50 ft. The bedroom (carpet), baths (tile) and hall saddle (D-M-BED2) already break the field.
evidence.expected: Gap 3/16 in minimum (the 5/16 in used is conservative and fine); the note should state the LVP field (~841 SF), not the whole floor.
evidence.method: A-603 p152 areas; baseline takeoff.json floor_finishes; pdftotext of the Karndean guide (kd.txt lines 118-126, 84-86).

findings.proposed_fix: Reword lvp_flooring.md: 'one field of ~841 SF; 3/16 in is the minimum, 5/16 in kept as margin' (or drop to 3/16 and the base/kick details follow).
